events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Caroline, or Change the Musical
events.description: 8 performances | October 31 and November 6*, 7, 13, and 14 at 7:30pm | November 1, 8, and 15 at 2:00pm *Friday, November 6 will include ASL interpretation and free tickets for Montgomery County residents! Full information at www.r-m-t.org/caroline-or-change Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. Image: Boris Ignatovich (Russian, 1899-1976), Composer Dmitri Shostakovich, from "Ignatovich, Soviet Avant-Garde", 1928, gelatin silver print, 16 H x 20 W in. events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

events.description: Tour the most haunted building in Frederick – the National Museum of Civil War Medicine on HALLOWEEN NIGHT! On the tour, staff and volunteers will share stories of Civil War embalmers, the building’s most infamous tenants, and their first-hand accounts of paranormal activity that have given the building its spooky reputation. In addition to a trip through the museum galleries, the tour provides exclusive access to the third floor where numerous sightings have occurred. You are invited to bring your own cameras and ghost-finding apps – who knows what you’ll capture! Flash photography and LIVE streaming are prohibited. Join Historic Annapolis: Very Superstitious! Paca House and Garden Tour: A History of Luck, Lore, and Beliefs
events.description: Discover the fascinating world of superstitions, folklore, and everyday beliefs that shaped life in centuries past. On this guided tour of the William Paca House and Garden, explore the origins of customs and practices once accepted as fact and, in some cases, still observed today. From household rituals to good-luck charms and protective practices, uncover the meanings behind these enduring traditions and learn how they influenced daily life. Join us for an engaging journey into the beliefs that helped people make sense of an uncertain world and discover how echoes of these old superstitions still linger today. At the conclusion of the tour, guests are invited to enjoy seasonal refreshments and share their favorite superstition! Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in October. To see times, visit our October event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Weather or private events may alter the tour route. Please dress for the weather. Advance registration recommended; space is limited. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? events.title: Madds Buckley
events.description: In an increasingly artificial world, singer-songwriter Madds Buckley is staying undeniably human. An RIAA Gold-certified artist with more than 2 million monthly listeners, Buckley pairs clear vocals with unexpected melodies and a deep-rooted instinct for storytelling. Her music sits at a unique intersection: honest, accessible, and highly personal storytelling that often incorporates themes found in anime, video games, and narrative-driven media. Even at its most fantastical, her music never loses sight of what’s real. Following My Love Is Sick, Buckley continues to evolve with a new run of releases, including “Overboard,” “Concept Without Proof,” and “Human to You,” ahead of her forthcoming album Simple Binary and a Complex Phrase (out October 16). Expanding her sonic and thematic scope more than ever before, the album interrogates the artificial to get to the heart of what’s most real: loving, losing, and persevering through the pain. Madds Buckley has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 per ticket goes to supporting Conscious Alliance’s mission to end hunger nationwide and feed families in need.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Ranger Tours at Peirce Mill
events.description: Step inside Peirce Mill, a rare surviving 19th-century gristmill in Rock Creek Park, and discover how waterpower once supported daily life in Washington, DC. Built in the 1820s, the mill served local farmers by grinding grain into flour and cornmeal. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. events.description: Three DC-area acts take the stage for an evening of pop-rock energy and local legacy. The Speaks, active from 1997 to 2009, broke down barriers with anthemic music and legendary live shows, earning radio play on DC101 and selling out five consecutive 9:30 Club shows. Signed to Warner Music (Asia) in 2005, their single "High" received unprecedented worldwide airplay and remains covered by artists globally; still streamed over 1 million times monthly. Crash Boom Bang returns to the stage in 2026 after a decade away, reuniting the band that helped define DC's pop-rock chapter. They cut their teeth at Jammin' Java, packing the house show after show before touring alongside Plain White T's, Mayday Parade, and Gin Blossoms. Their 2012 EP These Wild Things earned film and TV placements, while their "V.I.P." music video surpassed 300,000 views. Produced by Tom Higgenson of Plain White T's, their debut Gold Rush set the tone for their signature anthemic hooks and high-energy sound. Now they return home for one night only. Kill For Sushi, the rebranded project of Angie Pepa and former Wandering Lies bandmates, brings a new musical direction. As Wandering Lies, they won four battle-of-the-bands competitions and earned 2021 WAMA nominations. Their new album arrives in 2026. Jammin' Java celebrates these hometown forces in Fairfax County, Virginia.

In 2005, The Speaks signed a deal with Warner Music (Asia) with the "Life's a Joke" album release in the Philippines. The second single of the album, "High" received an unprecedented amount of worldwide airplay and is still being covered today from artists all over the world on YouTube. The Speaks released their final EP, "This is the Time" in 2008 and was distributed by Universal Music (Asia). From sharing the stage with national acts, to having their music videos receive heavy rotation on MTV Asia and MYX Music Channel, and still to this day being streamed over 1 million times monthly, The Speaks left their mark on the music scene and plenty of hangovers all over the world. events.title: Unfossilizing African Art
events.description: Presented after extensive research, this exhibition recontextualizes African material culture objects held in the GW Collection for nearly 50 years. Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.description: A Quiet Space A Silent Retreat for Rest, Reflection & Renewal Before the gatherings. Before the shopping. Before the travel. Before the expectations. Before the season asks you to give so much of yourself, give yourself a place to pause. A Quiet Space is a gentle, intentionally designed silent retreat at Harmony Hills in Deale, Maryland, created for rest, reflection, and renewal. For a few hours, step away from the noise and demands of everyday life and enter a quieter space—one where you don't have to perform, produce, solve, or explain. Simply be. Through intentional silence, reflection, stillness, and spaciousness, you'll have an opportunity to reconnect with yourself and notice what may be asking for your attention. You don't need to arrive with a particular intention. You don't need to know what you need. You don't need to have anything figured out. Just come as you are. Whether you're moving through a season of change, carrying something unseen, feeling the weight of the upcoming holidays, or simply longing for a little more quiet in your life, there is room for you here. A Quiet Space includes: • Guided moments of reflection • Periods of intentional silence • Time for personal rest and stillness • Gentle grounding practices • Space to journal, reflect, or simply be • A peaceful setting at Harmony Hills Choose the amount of quiet that feels right for you. events.title: African American Quilt Documentation Day in DC
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts - Great Hall
events.address: 1250 New York Ave NW, Washington, DC 20005-3970
events.description: WASHINGTON, DC — The African American Quilt Documentation Study Group (AAQDSG) will host a FREE quilt documentation event in Washington, DC on Sunday, November 1, 2026, inviting the African American community to bring family quilts in to be documented, preserved, and honored as part of our shared history. Date: Sunday, November 1, 2026 Time: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM Location: National Museum of Women in the Arts, 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005 Cost: Free — pre-registration required (time slots are limited) Since the 1980s, quilt documentation has been used to preserve family legacies and record the social, cultural, and artistic significance of quilts. African American family quilts have historically been excluded from this process. Most exist today with no documented history of the quilt or its maker — what's known has been passed down orally and never recorded. "Documentation is how we hold onto that," said A'donna Richardson, Director of AAQDSG. "It's an act of honoring our ancestors, of making sure the work of the quilt maker's hands is remembered. It's a way of saying: our ancestors mattered, what they made matters, and the stories tied to their quilts matter." The process reaches beyond individual families. Documented quilts become part of the historical record that scholars, museums, and researchers rely on to understand African American creativity, survival, faith, and community. Without this work, those stories remain untold and the historical record remains misrepresented and incomplete. We are encouraging the African American community to bring their family quilts, in whatever condition (the older, the better), to the November 1 event to have them photographed and documented, and to share the stories behind them. YOU MUST REGISTER to attend: https://aaqdsg.org/events If all appointment slots are filled, send your name and contact information to afamquilydoc@aadqsg.org. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. ​ In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four working in a service job to a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. ​ Caroline, or Change is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. It is a story that will open minds. It is a story that will change theatergoers

events.title: Corey Arceneaux & the Zydeco Hot Peppers
events.description: 6:00pm • $20 • Tickets on Eventbrite and at the door if available Corey Arceneaux and the Zydeco Hot Peppers Corey Arceneaux and the Zydeco Hot Peppers bring the heat of Southwest Louisiana straight to the DMV with an electrifying mix of authentic zydeco, Creole rhythms, and dance-floor energy. A Louisiana native, Corey Arceneaux is a powerhouse accordionist and bandleader whose sound is rooted in tradition and shaped by legends like Clifton Chenier and Buckwheat Zydeco—who also served as a mentor and friend. With five studio albums and decades of international touring, Corey delivers a show that’s as genuine as it is high-energy. Now based in Virginia, Corey has assembled a seasoned all-star lineup of regional players who live and breathe roots music. The Zydeco Hot Peppers feature Ben Holmes (drums), a veteran of global zydeco tours and DC favorites; Doug Bell (guitar), a staple of the East Coast roots scene; Gene Monroe (bass), whose credits span blues, rock, and beyond; and Pat Clark (frottoir), a multi-instrumentalist with deep ties to New Orleans traditions. Together, they create a groove that’s equal parts bayou party and dancehall throwdown. Whether it’s a festival stage, club night, or Mardi Gras celebration, Corey Arceneaux and the Zydeco Hot Peppers turn every performance into a full-on Louisiana experience—accordion-driven, rhythm-heavy, and impossible to sit still for. Whether you're familiar with Día de Muertos traditions or discovering them for the first time, we invite you to join us in celebrating the rich cultural heritage behind this occasion and the universal importance of remembering those who came before us. Bring your friends, bring your family, and come spend some time with your neighbors as we celebrate life, memory, and community in the heart of Brunswick.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.description: A series of immersive outdoor mindfulness sessions designed to help you slow down, cultivate curiosity, and deepen your connection to nature and history. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. events.title: Re-Leaf Agency
events.description: A Multisensory Performance Prompting Reflection and Action Re-Leaf Agency invites you into an immersive environment of lush movement, rich sounds, provocative text, and larger-than-life video projections of trees, mushrooms, ferns, wildflowers, and streams spanning multiple surfaces. The performers summon you into the woods, amplifying all manner of small and precious flora and fauna, to reveal a needed refuge. Re-Leaf Agency is a recruitment session disguised as a performance, or maybe it’s a performance disguised as a recruitment session. Either way, this is the last time in 2026 when you can join the Agency to become a keeper of the good. Three Re-Leaf Agents - two dancers and a recruitment officer - implore you to join them in navigating the turbulent times in which we find ourselves. Amidst the anxiety of an unraveling democracy and the impacts of a changing climate, Re-Leaf Agency rekindles hope by taking the long view of the natural world. This multimedia piece is the culmination of several years documenting a sliver of earth on the edge of Maryland’s South Mountain, during which time MAD Dance director Kit Clark experienced the solace of non-human time while walking and witnessing the land. Re-Leaf Agency shares that profound experience with others. Dancers Amanda Comi and Jeanna Riscigno join Clark in this one-of-a-kind performance.

events.title: Rockville Musical Theatre presents “Caroline, or Change”
events.description: 8 performances | Oct. 31 and Nov. 6*, 7, 13 & 14 at 7:30 p.m. | Nov. 1, 8 & 15 at 2 p.m. Set in one of the most pivotal times in America’s history, the Tony-nominated Caroline, or Change is riveting, moving, and awe-inspiring. Featuring a virtuosic score by Jeanine Tesori (Shrek The Musical, Thoroughly Modern Millie), it blends blues, gospel and traditional Jewish melodies, creating a breathtaking medium for Kushner’s provocative and personal story. In 1963, the Gellman family and their African-American maid, Caroline, live in sleepy Lake Charles, Louisiana. Caroline is drifting through life as a single mother of four, working in a service job for a white family. A fragile, yet beautiful friendship develops between the young Gellman son, Noah, and Caroline. Noah’s stepmother, Rose, unable to give Caroline a raise, tells Caroline that she may keep the money that Noah leaves in his pockets. Caroline balks and refuses to take money from a child, but her own children desperately need food, clothing and shoes. Outside of the laundry room, some of the greatest social advancements that the country has seen are being set in motion, and change is knocking on the door. Caroline, or Change, produces a valuable theatrical experience that continues to thrill audiences the world over. It is a story that must be shared and will touch hearts. events.title: Tapping into Timelessness - $45
events.description: Who hasn’t counted down the days to an upcoming vacation, waiting for the fun to begin? But what if we didn’t have to wait for a break from everyday life to experience deeper presence, connection, and joy? We spend much of our lives organizing ourselves around time—watching the clock, managing schedules, meeting deadlines, and trying to fit more into already-full days. Yet we also experience moments when our usual relationship with time seems to disappear. We become absorbed in something we love, deeply connected, or fully present to the moment. What if we could experience more of life not by cramming more into our time, but by changing how we inhabit it? In this experiential workshop, we’ll consider how our state of consciousness can shape our experience of time. Through discussion, reflection, and guided meditation, we’ll reconnect with moments of timelessness, explore what allows us to move beyond ordinary “clock time,” and discover how shifting our state of being can transform everyday experiences. Ultimately, you will leave with intentions for tapping into timelessness more intentionally and creating more space for the experiences that bring richness, meaning, and joy to your life.

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow-Olney Theatre
events.description: Olney audiences were blown away in 2025, when we invited Synetic Theater to perform their award-winning, wordless version of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream . Now they’re back, but this time they’re tackling a story with classic American roots in the intimate confines of Olney Theatre Center’s 150-seat Theatre Lab. In the haunted village of Sleepy Hollow, the past refuses to stay buried. Years after a brutal Revolutionary War encounter leaves a Hessian soldier beheaded and his beloved horse slain, the fallen rider returns as the legendary Headless Horseman—an apparition stalking the shadowed forests in search of what was taken from him. Inspired by Washington Irving’s classic tale, Sleepy Hollow reimagines the familiar legend as a haunting story of love, guilt, revenge, and redemption. Blending supernatural horror with theatrical spectacle, it asks whether the true monsters are the spirits who haunt us—or the deeds we would rather forget. By Washington Irving Adapted by Nathan Weinberger Directed by Paata Tsikurishvili Choreographed by Irina Tsikurishvili Due to the layout of the Mulitz-Gudelsky Theatre Lab, late seating is at the discretion of the House Manager. Those exiting the theatre during the performance will not be re-admitted while the performance is in progress.

Aligning in New Orleans during Jazz Fest, The Nth Power's electric live performances have floored audiences ever since. Following their breakout 2013 EP Basic Minimum Skills Test, the band released two acclaimed studio albums and two live albums, earning national coverage in Relix, Modern Drummer, Glide, Paste, and Sirius XM Radio. Their individual credentials include collaborations with Beyoncé, Snarky Puppy, Maceo Parker, Dumpstaphunk, and John Brown's Body. "It's my dream team," said bandleader Glaspie. "Each one of us is a songwriter, so when we get together, everything becomes that much stronger." Their inspirational sets have floored audiences at Electric Forest, High Sierra, Peachfest, North Coast Music Festival, and Hulaween. Maintaining New Orleans as their spiritual home, the celebratory essence of that city's music culture is palpable in each performance. Something magical is happening in this band. Jammin' Java welcomes The Nth Power to near Fairfax County, Virginia.

The exhibition is part of a University of Maryland Arts for All-funded project aimed at engaging students in science communication through art, increasing awareness of insect biodiversity and ecological roles, fostering collaboration across disciplines, evaluating changes in attendee knowledge, attitudes, and intentions, and contributing to a replicable arts-based model for conservation education. The exhibition will highlight six Maryland insect species that are included on Maryland’s List of Rare, Threatened, and Endangered Animals . Original works created through the exhibition’s two different open calls will be displayed alongside science-based information about insect ecological roles, insect habitats, and key conservation actions. events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. events.title: Forbidden
events.description: FORBIDDEN: Godfathers in the Bay Area metal scene, Forbidden have returned with their first album in 16 years to unleash 12 fierce, uncompromising, and supremely progressive songs which signal an almighty return. Forbidden will be released by BLKIIBLK Records on ________and charts a defiant journey through scything riffs, incredible melodies, 24 karat lead guitars, simply thunderous drums and bass, plus the studio debut of Norman Skinner (Niviane & Imagika) whose soaring vocals elevate the material to unprecedented levels. Conceived by founder and guitarist Craig Locicero alongside his creative brother, drummer Chris Kontos, the foundational energy of bassist Matt Camacho, the versatility and poise of guitarist Jeremy Von Epp, and Skinner’s voracious fresh approach, Forbidden sees the band arriving at their finest hour with their richest-ever line-up. With Skinner stepping up to take on lyrical duties, Forbidden takes a fierce and uncompromising look into the eyes of our times without taking sides, instead imploring people to recognize the false conflicts created by the current society and how they can conquer and rise above them. Take the blistering roar of “Single Point Failure”, the beautiful orchestral savagery of “Flower of Life”, and the relentless charge of “Burning The Lungs Of Earth.” There’s also the mid-paced brooding power of “Psyclops,” the twisting, winding power force of “Sycophantasy” featuring guest vocals from Mastodon’s Brann Dailor, and a thunderous ode to women “The Burden” featuring guest vocals from Kayla Dixon. In addition, Forbidden pay homage to classic American heavy metal band Savatage in the shape of a malevolent and mesmeric cover of “Sirens”, which embraces Greek mythology. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: West Asia: A New American Grand Strategy in the Middle East
events.description: Attend In-Person Attend Online Please join the Middle East Policy Forum, in partnership with the Sigur Center for Asian Studies, on November 3 to welcome Mohammed Soliman, author of West Asia: A New American Grand Strategy in the Middle East. Dr. Alyssa Ayres, Dean of the Elliott School of International Affairs, will deliver opening remarks. Mohammed Soliman argues in his book that it is time for the United States to move decisively away from nation-building and get back to the business of order-building. To do so will require zooming out, in both geographical and historical terms, to build a new regional order across ‘West Asia’ – from the Middle East to South Asia, connecting Europe to the Indo-Pacific via the Mediterranean and Red Seas. Working with India, Italy, Greece, France, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Japan, the UK, and the United Arab Emirates, among others, he shows how the United States could lock in a new balance of power in the Eurasian supercontinent to offset Chinese and Russian efforts to disrupt the status quo and create a rival system. This new strategy rests on three layered coalitions — geostrategic, hard-power, and geo-technological — that together can anchor a stable order stretching from the Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean. But this will require a fundamental shift in U.S. grand strategy, with ‘West Asia’ at its core. events.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh? Film Screening
events.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California, was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when a Palestinian American, Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite clear evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. Unfolding like a detective thriller, the film weaves archival footage, firsthand testimony, and new reporting to expose the violent fundamentalist networks behind the attack and the institutional failures that protected them. As the investigation deepens, the story widens to reveal how the extremist ideology that fueled Odeh’s murder did not disappear - it evolved, gaining traction and legitimacy in the modern political landscape. Directed by SMPA Professors Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans, a Jewish American and a Palestinian American, Who Killed Alex Odeh? is both a gripping cold-case pursuit and a timely examination of political violence, asking what it means when acts of terror go unresolved, and how justice denied continues to shape the world we live. The screening will be held on November 3 at 6 p.m. in the MPA 5th Floor Studio.

A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. The story of “A More Perfect Union” begins in Boston, 1773 and ends at the Constitutional Convention in Philadelphia, 1787. The play covers the critical and tempestuous time in our nation’s history in which revolution, war, and a failed attempt at self-governing finally led to the writing of the U.S. Constitution and the birth of our country as we know it today. events.title: BME Department Seminar
events.description: Join the Department of Biomedical Engineering for their upcoming seminar featuring Dr. Simiao Niu, an assistant professor at Rutgers University! He will be presenting "Battery-free Wireless Bioelectronic Network for Effective Chronic Disease Management." Abstract: 60% of the US population live with at least one chronic disease. These diseases and associated comorbidities are now the leading causes of death. Effective management of complex chronic diseases requires body-wide, long-term, accurate, and continuous monitoring of multiple physiological signals from wearable devices to precisely determine the pathological state. These wearable physiological signal monitoring can dramatically reduce the demand of physician visiting and increase patients’ engagement and treatment adherence rate. Although wearable bioelectronic devices have shown huge potential in chronic disease management, existing technology still mostly relies on rigid chip components, where the interface between chips and skin/tissue has been a bottleneck that limits the system performance (noise, robustness etc). To address these challenges, my group's research has been involved in the exploration of rational system design concepts, material and device fabrication innovation, tailored algorithms, and energy harvesting to enable a closed-loop wireless bioelectronic network that targets next-generation chronic disease management. In this talk, I will discuss my group's efforts in building this technology platform.

events.title: Camp One Heartland
events.description: Camp One Heartland is a solo exhibition by Tye DuSold-O’Connor archiving documentation of one of the world’s first nonprofit summer camps designated to supporting and empowering youth affected by HIV and AIDS, eventually transforming into a vital beacon of safety, liberation and eutopia for LGBTQ+ youth across the country. After its inaugural session in the summer of 1993 and many more held at different campsites across the country, Camp One Heartland found its permanent residence in Willow River, Minnesota. Over the next three decades it broadened its reach to provide summer camp sessions for youth experiencing housing instability, LGBTQ+ youth, and specifically trans youth. Tye attended Camp One Heartland as both a camper in 2022 and a counselor in 2024, and found these experiences indescribably transformative to them and their queer identity. Quite suddenly, Camp One Heartland shut down permanently in the fall of 2024 due to financial issues. Former campers, counselors and staff have been unable to return to the site since. While camp counseling in the summer of 2024, Tye took hundreds of photos of the camp, its people, and its experiences. These serve as some of the last images taken during the lifetime of Camp One Heartland. events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. events.title: Demo-ing, Sampling, Lip-Syncing: Commercial Misogynoir in Post-Disco EDM
events.description: Join the GW Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) Program for an exciting talk from Visiting Assistant Professor Eva Pensis! Across the late 20th century, the popular music industry faced a series of scandals in live performance with the widespread use of lip-syncing. Following the advent of recorded sound, the commercial use of lip-sync in the popular music industry sought to divide the recorded performance from the performer with the aim of controlling both, most often eliding the visual presence of African American musicians while profiting from their sonic contributions. Framed by the media theorist Moya Bailey's concept of "misogynoir," this presentation considers the case of Black Box, an Italian post-disco house music band from the 1980s who stole and misattributed the vocal demos of Martha Wash (a noted musician and vocalist from The Weather Girls and Two Tons o’ Fun) for their debut album. The ensuing crisis of representation that lip-syncing indexes forms the basis for this talk's investigation into the popular music industry's predation on African American women's song following the infamous demolition of disco and the digital quest to strip sound from song. RSVP online.

events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

Humanities in Asia: Going Beyond Make-Do-the Reshaping of a Chinese Operatic Tradition in Taiwan
events.description: Kunqu, a 600-year-old form of Chinese opera known for its poetic lyrics and refined singing, was among the first Chinese art forms UNESCO recognized as a "Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity" in 2001. The story of how Kunqu survived the political upheavals of the twentieth century runs not only through state-sponsored troupes in China but also through communities of devoted amateur singers, known as quyou (曲友), who carried the tradition to Taiwan. This talk follows these enthusiasts from their roots in Mainland China to their postwar lives in Taiwan, where they kept Kunqu alive through informal singing gatherings long before it was celebrated as world heritage. When cultural exchanges across the Taiwan Strait reopened, amateurs and professionals on both sides began collaborating on performances, training, preservation, and documentation, turning a private pastime into a shared project of heritage-making. Drawing on the experiences of Taiwan-based practitioners, the talk shows how this cross-strait collaboration reshaped Kunqu as a heritage for Sinophone audiences and how a common love for an art form built networks that reached beyond politics while still raising questions about cultural identity. Free lunch will be offered at this talk. Doors will open no sooner than 15 minutes before the start time. events.description: Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare. This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps! We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls. Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside? Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation? Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure. Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by. End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book. Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.
events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. events.description: Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare. This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps! We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls. Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside? Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation? Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure. Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by. End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book. Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.
events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Come along to hear about the ghosts and spirits that still haunt these streets…if you dare. This is a family-friendly ghost tour through Georgetown to see this exclusive neighborhood’s darker side. Stroll among the historic streets, manicured gardens, and Victorian row houses as you hear stories and deep, dark secrets about DC’s finest neighborhood’s forgotten past. The October 31 tour will include a special haunted light show at the Exorcist steps! We will see one of the most haunted and historic buildings in Washington, DC, the Old Stone House. A pre-Revolutionary home whose original builder may still roam the halls. Look up at old porches painted Haint Blue to keep out the spirits from crossing over the porch. But what if the spirit was already inside? Find out what happened at boarding schools turned hospitals during the American Civil War. Can you still hear the screams of amputations with no sedation? Walk past the historic house whose lights turned off every night at the same time; a nanny’s rules enforced long after her departure. Meet an eccentric man who built stairs to nowhere, slept in a coffin and refused to add electricity to his 1799 home. Hear why one of our guides refuses to lead this tour because he has been stalking her for 10 years, flickering lights when she walks by. End the tour at the Exorcist Stairs, featured in The Exorcist, and hear the true story that inspired a Georgetown student to write the book. Meet your guide outside 3051 M St NW at the Old Stone House. The tour ends at the top of Exorcist Steps at 36th and Prospect St NW Tour Duration: 1.5 Hours Walking Tour. Tours are available nightly at 7pm and 8pm.
events.title: Ghosts of Georgetown & Exorcist Steps Haunted Walking Tour

events.description: Experiencing history through outdoor mindfulness at Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House. About the Session: The sessions are approximately 90-minutes long and are conducted in relative silence. They include warm-ups, centering, and breathing exercises to connect participants to their bodies and the world around them. These are followed by a walk and an extended sit which encourages participants to become more fully open and present to their surroundings. We conclude with a returning ritual and a chance to reflect on the experience. This time in nature will not be strenuous; most abilities can be accommodated. All ages are welcomed but children under 16 must be accompanied by an adult. Important Arrival & Check-In Details Check-In Location: All participants must check in at Woodlawn, regardless of session topic. Timing: Sessions start promptly at 12:00 PM (Sundays). Please arrive early to ensure a timely start. Duration: Approximately 90 minutes. Fall Schedule & Locations Sunday, October 11 | Woodlawn Sunday, October 25 | Pope-Leighey House Sunday, November 1 | Woodlawn Sunday, November 8 | Pope-Leighey House Tickets & Policies Price: $30 per ticket. All purchases directly support the preservation of this historic site. Weather: Programs take place rain or shine.
events.title: Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House: Canopy of Discovery
